summary.value: The Twentse, known in German as the Kraienkopp, comes from the border country between the Netherlands and Germany. Breeders made it in the late 1800s by crossing local hens with Malay fowl, then adding silver duckwing Leghorn blood. Dutch shows first saw it in 1920, and German shows in 1925. The bird has yellow skin and a small walnut comb, with bright red wattles and earlobes, and comes in silver, gold and several other colors. Roosters weigh about 6 pounds and hens about 4 pounds. Hens lay up to around 200 off-white eggs a year, go broody and raise chicks well. The Twentse is active, alert and independent, with a hint of Malay fire, though it tames if raised by hand. It forages very well and stands up to cold, so it suits free range keepers.
